results.reason: The memo never mentions the Delivery and Logistics Schedule's 'Delivery Date' definition. It does not identify the ship-from-plant versus Rochester-delivery conflict or the loss of remedies for transit delays.
There is no recommendation to conform the Schedule's Delivery Date definition to the MSA. Nor does the memo address which document controls on conflict for that issue.

Issue 2 identifies that MSA §4.3 covers all housings and similar components worldwide, against the Term Sheet's Series 7 / U.S. limit. It explains the effect on non-U.S. plants and alternative suppliers and recommends narrowing to Series 7 Housings in the U.S.

Issue 3 identifies that §15.2 lets Verdane assign without consent, including to a competitor, while Harlow needs consent. It explains the supply and confidential Specifications risks and recommends prior written consent, a competitor bar and a change-of-control termination right.

Issue 1 identifies that Amendment §2.1 and §2.2 remove gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the §11.2 exclusions, subjecting them to the 12-month-fees cap. It recommends rejecting the change and restoring the original exclusions.
The memo states that §11.1 caps liability at fees paid in the prior 12 months and that §11.2 excludes gross negligence, willful misconduct and the §10.1 IP Indemnity.
The memo cites Term Sheet §3.1 (Series 7 Housings only, within the United States) and uses it as the baseline for comparing MSA §4.3.

The memo states New York law governs under MSA §16.1 and includes assumptions and open fact questions. It cites no cases or statutes, and flags its New York public-policy point as needing confirmation.

The memo is structured as a partner memo with a bottom line. Each issue gives where, why it matters and a recommended fix, issues are explicitly ordered by priority, and there is an assumptions and open points section.
The memo states the Term Sheet is used only as evidence of the deal. It expressly treats the 3-year term and 45-day payment terms as non-defects.
Section citations are accurate and party benefits are correctly stated. No fabricated authority appears, and the one general legal proposition is flagged as needing confirmation.
